title: Handicap-accessible Lots at HDB and URA-managed Car Parks
what_it_is: Handicap-accessible Lots at HDB and URA-managed Car Parks

sections.label: Accessible parking lot requirements
sections.summary: Developments with over 10 parking lots must provide accessible lots at stated ratios, with over 6,800 such lots in HDB and URA car parks.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: Developments with more than 10 parking lots are required to provide one accessible lot for every 50 lots of the first 100 lots and one accessible lot for every subsequent 200 lots or part thereof.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: There are currently more than 6,800 accessible parking lots across public car parks managed by HDB and URA.

sections.label: More accessible lots and code review
sections.summary: HDB and URA will consider more accessible lots based on feedback and feasibility, and BCA reviews the Code about every five years, next in 2023.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: HDB and URA will also consider providing more accessible lots in their car parks based on public feedback and where it is feasible to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: BCA reviews the Code requirements about once every five years.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for National Development (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for National Development)
sentences.text: BCA will commence the next review in 2023.

sections.label: Planning ahead with buffer
sections.summary: It is better to plan ahead with a buffer than to catch up, and these will be looked into in the review.

sentences.speaker: Mr Seah Kian Peng (Marine Parade)
sentences.text: And it is better to plan ahead and have a little bit of buffer, rather than having to do a bit of catch-up.

sentences.speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
sentences.text: We will look into these in our review.
